facts.raw_span: A patient in their 70s presented with dyspnea and fatigue
No history of structural heart disease or hypertension
Medical history significant for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed 4 years ago, treated with 8 courses of chemotherapy
Blood pressure: 96/54 mm Hg
Heart rate: 56 bpm
Serum troponin I: 0.04 ng/mL (normal value, <0.02 ng/mL)
NT-proBNP: 3896.83 pg/mL (normal value, <100 pg/mL)
Present ECG shows prolonged P-wave duration (180 milliseconds), positive-negative biphasic P wave in leads II, III, and aVF, with shortened or disappeared PR segment
Transthoracic echocardiogram: Revealed diffuse medium masses in the right atrium, measuring approximately 50 mm × 22 mm
PET-CT scan: Showed significantly increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium

concepts.why: The patient has a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and presents with a mass in the right atrium, suggesting cardiac involvement by lymphoma.
The patient presents with hypotension, elevated NT-proBNP, and a mass in the right atrium, suggesting cardiac tamponade.
The patient presents with elevated NT-proBNP, prolonged P-wave duration, and increased metabolic activity along the pericardium, suggesting constrictive pericarditis.
The patient has a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and presents with a mass in the right atrium and increased metabolic activity along the pericardium, suggesting lymphomatous pericarditis.

rationales.F03: History of lymphoma increases the likelihood of cardiac lymphoma and lymphomatous pericarditis.
rationales.F07: Elevated NT-proBNP suggests cardiac dysfunction, which could be due to cardiac lymphoma, cardiac tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, or lymphomatous pericarditis.
rationales.F08: ECG findings suggest atrial involvement, which could be due to cardiac lymphoma or lymphomatous pericarditis.
rationales.F09: Masses in the right atrium are highly suggestive of cardiac lymphoma.
rationales.F10: Increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium suggests lymphomatous involvement.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and the presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium, along with increased metabolic activity on PET-CT scan, strongly support Cardiac Lymphoma as the most specific diagnosis.
